source_snapshot.procedure: After requested log clearing, issue local `ipmitool mc reset cold`, issue OOB raw 0x06/0x02, then check BMC behavior.
source_snapshot.criteria: BMC resets successfully, its network disconnects once, and the host OS remains normal.
source_snapshot.script: Private bmc-cold-reset; 10 attended and 10 machine minutes.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; proposes one OOB high-level cold reset and a truncated `mc info` check after about 60 seconds, warning that OOB sessions drop.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION at HIGH risk; approve one reset method/path, same-target identity, alternate recovery, one bounded disconnect/reconnect, full BMC health and independent host OS/power continuity evidence.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Recognizes management interruption but does not resolve IB versus raw OOB execution, risks two resets, exposes credentials and provides no independent host-continuity proof.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly limits execution to one approved reset unless dual-path coverage is explicitly designed and requires alternate recovery plus host-invariance evidence.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Both listed commands perform a cold reset, so blindly following the procedure creates two service interruptions while the criterion expects one disconnect. Transport coverage and reset count must be explicitly separated: one reset can test recovery, while a second needs independent approval and a restored baseline.

original_test_intent: Verify an approved BMC cold reset method causes the expected single management interruption and bounded recovery while host power, OS and workload remain healthy.
original_method: Verify same-target IB/OOB mapping and choose the approved reset path/count; capture BMC/LAN/host/console/log baselines; issue exactly one authorized cold reset; time disconnect and recovery; revalidate identity and full BMC health; independently prove host continuity; retain all evidence and use alternate recovery on timeout.
manual_activity: The owner approves the dedicated target, reset count/path, window, timeout and recovery plan; an operator remains available on an alternate console and owns the final verdict.
required_inputs: Approved high-level or raw reset method
safety_requirements: Execute only the approved reset count
Do not run both source commands by default
Expect but bound one management disconnect
Never power-cycle the host as implicit recovery
Stop on repeated disconnect or identity drift
Never retry an ambiguous reset automatically
agent_execution_scope: Verify target, idle state and recovery path
Archive evidence and report without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve reset method, path, count and maintenance window
Review timeout, repeated disconnect or host anomaly
Authorize any second reset or re-execution

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its OOB `mc reset cold` expresses the target operation but drops the source IB/raw path question, embeds credentials and truncates post-reset health evidence.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use one protected vendor-supported `mc reset cold` or documented raw 0x06/0x02 through the approved path, then perform bounded recovery, full identity/health and independent host-continuity checks.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The cold-reset intent and 10/10-minute envelope are preserved; the two listed reset commands are not silently executed as two resets.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a timeline of approval, baseline, reset response, management loss, first reachability, authenticated readiness, service health, host power/OS/workload observations and final log deltas.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines reset count/path, alternate recovery, staged readiness and independent host checks while preserving logs.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A returned reset response and one `mc info` call cannot prove a single disconnect, complete service recovery or uninterrupted host operation.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The command response may be lost because the BMC resets before replying; that ambiguity must be resolved by the external timeline, not by resending the reset.

project_override_considerations: The Project must state whether IB and OOB are alternative ways to trigger one reset or separately required runs. If both are required, each needs separate approval, baseline restoration and disconnect chronology. Raw 0x06/0x02 must be vendor-supported for the target firmware.
expected_evidence: Approval, target identity, chosen method/path/count and idle-operation proof
Alternate recovery and baseline BMC/LAN/host/console health
Reset request/response and single disconnect/reconnect timeline
Post-recovery target identity and complete BMC service health
Independent host power/OS/workload continuity and preserved log deltas
Retry-free recovery audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: All source fields target BMC cold reset. The presence of two trigger paths and a one-disconnect criterion creates an execution-count ambiguity that must be approved, but not a competing test objective.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Reset method, count, timeout and recovery path are obtainable project inputs. Execution becomes BLOCKED if alternate recovery or safe same-target/host-continuity verification cannot be established.

review_improvement: Prevents an accidental double cold reset and makes the one-disconnect and host-continuity criteria measurable without erasing diagnostic evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A BMC can answer ping before IPMI, KVM, sensors and event services are ready, so reachability alone is not recovery. Also, the reset connection may end before a completion response. A monotonic external observer plus staged authenticated health checks is required, and the trigger must never be repeated merely because the initiating session dropped as expected.
